dataset.name: rm_yields_1990plus.csv (wide) + rm_yields_1990plus_long.csv (long)
dataset.description: Real Saskatchewan RM crop yields, 1990-2025. WIDE (one crop per column) for stats/lookups; LONG (Crop in its own column) for PivotTables.

question_types.description: Filter to one crop in one year, then compute summary statistics with Excel functions.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Filter to Year = 2023. Compute the mean canola yield across all reporting RMs.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Compute the median canola yield for 2023.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compute the sample standard deviation of 2023 canola yield.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Compute Q1, Q3, and the IQR of 2023 canola yield.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Compute the 90th percentile of 2023 canola yield and explain what it means.
parts.answer: ≈ 50.44 bu/ac — 90% of reporting RMs yielded this or less.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Is the mean or median higher, and what does that say about the shape?
parts.answer: Median (35.5) > mean (33.9): slightly left-skewed — low-yield drought RMs pull the mean down.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Filter to Year = 2023. Compute the mean and median spring wheat yield.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Compute the sample standard deviation and variance of 2023 spring wheat. Units of variance?
parts.answer: sd ≈ 17.22 bu/ac; variance ≈ 296.5 (bu/ac)² — units are squared.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compute the min, max, and range of 2023 spring wheat yield.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Compute Q1, Q3, and IQR of 2023 spring wheat yield.

parts.label: e
parts.text: How many RMs reported a spring wheat yield in 2023?
parts.answer: ≈ 285 RMs (COUNT skips blanks; below the ~295 total rows).

question_types.description: Use COUNTIF, AVERAGEIF, COUNTIFS, XLOOKUP, and IF across the full unfiltered dataset.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Across all years and RMs, how many rows have canola yield strictly greater than 40 bu/ac?

parts.label: b
parts.text: What is the average canola yield in 2023 only? (Use AVERAGEIF on the Year column.)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compare average canola yield in 2010 vs 2021 (a drought year). Which is higher?

parts.label: d
parts.text: Use a two-criteria lookup to find the canola yield in RM 1 in 2023.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Write a formula classifying each row's canola yield as Low (<20), Medium (20–40), or High (>40).
parts.answer: Low / Medium / High in a new column.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many rows report a lentil yield (non-blank cells in the Lentils column)?

parts.label: b
parts.text: What is the average barley yield across all years in RM 100?

parts.label: c
parts.text: How many rows have canola above 40 AND spring wheat above 45 in the same RM-year?

parts.label: d
parts.text: Use a lookup to find the spring wheat yield in RM 100 in 2023.

parts.label: e
parts.text: In how many rows is canola above the overall average canola yield?

question_types.description: Use the LONG file (rm_yields_1990plus_long.csv). Crop is its own column, so you can pivot by crop.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Using the long file: PivotTable of average yield for each crop in 2023 (Year in Filter = 2023, Crop on Rows, Yield as Average). Rank crops high to low.
parts.answer: Lentils ~1314 (lb/ac!), Oats ~71, Barley ~55, Spring Wheat ~43, Peas ~34, Canola ~34, Durum ~30, Flax ~20.
parts.formula: Year → Filter (2023); Crop → Rows; Yield → Values (Average)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Why does Lentils appear far larger than every other crop?
parts.answer: Lentils are in lb/ac, all others in bu/ac — a unit difference, not higher yield. Don't rank it against the bu/ac crops.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Filter Unit to bu/ac. Which crop is highest, which lowest, in 2023?
parts.answer: Oats highest (~71 bu/ac), Flax lowest (~20 bu/ac).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Long file: PivotTable with Year on Rows, Crop on Columns, Yield as Average, Unit filtered to bu/ac. In a typical recent year, which crops are highest/lowest?
parts.answer: Oats and Barley highest; Flax lowest.
parts.formula: Year → Rows, Crop → Columns, Yield → Values (Average), Unit → Filter (bu/ac)

parts.label: b
parts.text: From the same grid, compare canola in 2021 vs 2023. How large is the drought gap?
parts.formula: Read the Canola column for rows 2021 and 2023

parts.label: c
parts.text: Reading down the columns, which single year is a drought year (all crops low at once)?
parts.formula: Scan the grid for a uniformly low row

question_types.description: Create and interpret histograms, box plots, and time-series line charts.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Filter to 2023. Create a histogram of canola yield across RMs (10–15 bins), titled with labelled axes.
parts.answer: Slightly left-skewed, centred ~34–36, low-end drought outliers.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Is the 2023 canola distribution symmetric, left-skewed, or right-skewed? Any outliers?
parts.answer: Slightly left-skewed; a few low-yield RM outliers.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Create a box plot comparing Canola, Spring Wheat, and Barley in 2023. Which has the highest median? The most spread?
parts.answer: Barley highest median; spring wheat widest spread; low-end outliers on all three.
parts.formula: Insert → Statistical Chart → Box and Whisker

parts.label: a
parts.text: PivotTable of average canola yield by year, then a line chart 1990–2025. Is there a long-run upward trend? Why?
parts.answer: Yes — rising trend from better genetics/agronomy/equipment.
parts.formula: PivotTable Year→Rows, Canola→Average; Insert → Line Chart

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which years show sharp dips, and what do they correspond to?
parts.answer: Drought years, notably 2021 — weather shocks, not trend changes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Make a line chart of average spring wheat yield by year. Do wheat and canola move together?
parts.answer: Yes — both track growing-season weather, so they rise and fall together.
parts.formula: PivotTable Year→Rows, Spring Wheat→Average; Insert → Line Chart
